### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/automation/flow-template-token.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via FlowSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/automation/flow-template-token.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7a03de5edce39887fc6557bef857b5478fc647c2` — the merge of head `f88ed85f6d11a6c538ab1ba56c2a852162a31953` into base `404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7a03de5edce39887fc6557bef857b5478fc647c2 && git checkout 7a03de5edce39887fc6557bef857b5478fc647c2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc f88ed85f6d11a6c538ab1ba56c2a852162a31953 && git checkout -B drift-repro 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc && git merge --no-ff f88ed85f6d11a6c538ab1ba56c2a852162a31953

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f88ed85f6d11a6c538ab1ba56c2a852162a31953`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #23260 (body; triage `6147540471`, claim `6149208812`, report `6152617434`, ACCEPT `6152686934`), #21898 and the #19939 S7 report `6143212658` for context, PR #23319 (body, the one bot comment, 8-file list, the net diff `origin/main...f88ed85f6`, merge base `9c7cfbf0a`), the 41 check-runs on the head, and `origin/main` / the head by `git show` and `git grep`. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The narrowing, at both build doors — RIGHT, and exactly what triage ordered.** The only reader of the carve-out on `origin/main` was `builtinValueJudged:416` (`flow-node-config-refusals.ts`); the diff deletes that line, `carriesInterpolationToken` and `INTERPOLATION_TOKEN`, and nothing else in the tree named them (git grep, CHANGELOGs excluded). The deleted regex `/\{[^{}]+\}/` is the same grammar as `TEMPLATE_TOKEN` (`flow-template-token.ts:52`), so "every value the carve-out admitted" is a well-defined set and the new accept set is main's minus exactly that set at the keys a contract refuses. Both doors share the one judge: `FlowSchema`'s superRefine calls `flowNodeConfigRefusals`; `defineStack` parses `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` whose `flows` are `FlowSchema`; `registerFlow` parses first. The new pins hold the refusal at `nodes.1.config.limit` (FlowSchema), at `flows.0.nodes.1.config.limit` in the `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` 422 envelope (`defineStack`), and at `limit` through `AutomationEngine.registerFlow` plus the run (`config-parse.test.ts`). Nothing else is newly refused by construction: `absentAt`, the `whole` plugin-contract arm, `parsedWhen` (a body-less `loop`), region slots, `insideValueSlot`, `atOrInsideJudgedLedgerSlot` and `RUN_RESOLVED_KEYS` are untouched. The 1010-literal census (0 moved) is the dev's measurement, not re-run here; it is consistent with my grep: no docs page, lint rule or example asserts the carve-out, and the only text hits are release-owned CHANGELOG entries, untouched.

2. **The rule-finding class — RIGHT, declared.** A `notify` `templateData` with no `template` whose map carried a token was hidden by the carve-out (the rule anchors at `['templateData']`, `io-node-config.zod.ts:664`, and `authoredAt` of that path carried the token); it is now reported. That is inside "like any literal" (a token-free `templateData` map was refused by the rule on main), it is named in the changeset and the Acceptance notes, and it is not a double report: the value-slot judge's finding sits at `templateData.KEY`, a different defect at a different path.

3. **Exemption 1, the slot-judge paths — RIGHT and minimal.** `slotJudgeRefusedPaths` unions `flowNodeValueTemplateRefusals(...).path` and each `flowNodeTextSlotSources` entry whose `textSlotTemplateRefusal` is defined; the arm compares `ledgerPathOf(issue.path)`. The spellings meet: the contracts compose the same two judges (`celValueSlotSchema` adds at `[...refusal.path]`, `flowFilterSlotSchema` at `[...operand.path, ...refusal.path]`, `NotifyRecipientsSlotSchema` at `[index]`, the text slots at `[key]` and `['headers', name]`), and `ledgerPathOf`, `joinPath` and `operandPath` render `[n]` and `.seg` identically. Minimal: the value-slot judge refuses only strings matching `TEMPLATE_TOKEN`, and the text-slot judge a single-brace token or a double-brace hole over an unbound dollar root, which the deleted regex also matched, so the exempted set is a subset of what the carve-out already skipped: nothing is newly silenced against main. `registerFlow` and `objectstack validate` call both judges themselves, so one token at a value or text slot draws exactly one located finding there, the judge's, with its label and remedy; the pins hold that over six value slots and six text slots through `judgedAtTheDoors`, which composes exactly the three judges those doors call. At `FlowSchema.parse` and `defineStack` the result is parity with main (no finding, item ③ out-of-scope 1). The judges are asked once per config, lazily, only when a present value reaches the question.

4. **Exemption 2, the read-as-written preference — RIGHT and minimal.** `readAsWrittenKeys` is the ledger path of every issue marked `READ_AS_WRITTEN_PARAM` in the same parse (producers at head: `notifyLiteralRefusals` at `sourceObject`, `actorId`, `payload.*`; the `HTTP_LITERALS` keys at `[key]`; the whole `headers` map at `['headers']`). A non-marked issue at such a key is skipped and the marked one is judged. Without it, the Zod type issue at `timeoutMs` / `headers` would reach the `seen` dedupe first and replace the literal's remedy; with it, the key is refused once in the literal's words, as on main (pinned for `timeoutMs: '{t}'` and `headers: '{h}'`). Scope is exact: a token-free wrong-typed literal (`timeoutMs: 'soon'`) carries no marked issue and is still refused for its type (existing pin). The relative order (`isReadAsWrittenIssue` returns true before both exemptions, after membership / region / ledger-slot / run-resolved) is main's.

5. **Premise 1 — SOUND on `origin/main`.** `service-automation/src/builtin/template.ts` exports only `VariableMap`, `FlowTextTemplateError`, `textTemplateScope` and `renderTextSlot`; no non-test, non-comment caller of `interpolate(`, `interpolateString(` or `resolveToken(` remains in `service-automation/src` or `spec/src/automation`; `http-nodes.ts` parses `{ ...authored, signingSecret: held }` at `:234` before any `renderTextSlot` / `resolveValueSlot`. A token at a typed key was refused at every run that reached the node before this PR and still is; the build doors now say so first.

6. **Public surface — UNCHANGED, right.** The two deleted helpers were module-private (no `export`, no reader outside the file, no mention in `packages/spec/api-surface/**` or `api-surface-signatures.json`); `slotJudgeRefusedPaths`, `isReadAsWrittenIssue` and `ValueArmScope` are module-private too; `git diff origin/main...head -- packages/spec/api-surface*` is empty. The two imports the arm adds at module load create no new cycle (both judges import only `flow-node-expression-paths`, `context-tokens.zod` and `flow-template-token`, already in the arm's graph). Gate readings on the head: "Type Check · consumer gates" (runs `check:api-surface`) success; "Type Check · workspace" (runs `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, the one gate the dev could not measure locally) success.

7. **The corrected rationale, five places — TRUE.** `flow-template-token.ts` (the marker now says which issue speaks for the key), the value arm's docblocks and the ledger-slot docblock in `flow-node-config-refusals.ts`, the `FlowSchema` comment, the step-18 D3 entry's `surface` / `replacement` / `reason` / `acceptanceCriteria`, and the `registry.ts.template` order-85 fragment each state what holds: every builtin parses as authored; a token-carrying value is judged like any literal; a read-as-written key is refused once in the literal's words; a slot its own judge refuses is not re-judged; `signingSecret` is never judged; a token at a plain string key still registers. `registry.ts` is gitignored and rebuilt from the template plus entries, so nothing generated is owed; "Type Check · source gates" (`check:generated`) success. Non-blocking prose note: the `replacement` field's `http` clause ("and at an http node's durable and timeoutMs, which http once interpolated before it parsed, so a sole-token template there resolved to the declared type, with the literal's remedy") lost its main verb in the edit; it is not false and the entry's other three fields say the same thing plainly.

8. **Tests — RIGHT.** The removed CONTROL pinned the carve-out and is replaced, not weakened. Ablations A1 / A2 / A3 red as predicted and restored are the dev's measurements, consistent with the code (A2 fails because the exemption is load-bearing at slots whose path length equals the ledger segments, where `insideValueSlot` does not already skip).

9. **Check-runs on `f88ed85f6`:** 41, all `completed`: 35 success, 6 skipped (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix placeholder, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke opt-in, Temporal Conformance — path and opt-in skips), 0 failure, 0 in progress. Governed Surface Queue Guard success; none of the 8 paths is a governed surface.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23260-builtin-token-value-judged.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, the `**BREAKING**` banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, the marker `adr-0087: not-required (already-registered flow-builtin-node-config-values-refused)`, and a six-row FROM → TO table with the one-line fix (write the literal the key declares). RIGHT.
- **Level `minor` is right by ruling, not only by convention:** ADR-0087's 2026-09-13 (#18003) amendment, the level half — "Pre-GA, a metadata-facing retirement or break ships `minor`, carrying the BREAKING banner and its ADR-0087 disposition entry"; `.changeset/pre.json` is `pre` / `next`; the #21898 bullet this supersedes sits under `### Minor Changes` of `18.0.0-next.0`. The PR title carries the bang (`fix(spec)!:`).
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is right:** the diff publishes nothing new and widens nothing; it moves a refusal from the first run to the build doors. It is spelled in the closed-pair grammar on PR body line 2 and in the changeset; the claim comment's longer parenthetical is the claim's own text, settled by the seat's ACCEPT.
- **ADR-0087 `already-registered` is right:** the D3 entry `flow-builtin-node-config-values-refused` exists at the merge base and at HEAD (the check's own criterion for that disposition); no key is removed or renamed, so there is no tombstone and no D2 conversion can exist; amending the entry's text is the correct route because the upgrade guide and `spec-changes.json` are generated at publish from the registries (ADR-0087 D4 as amended 2026-10-09), so the amended text is what ships. "Check Changeset" (runs `check-adr-0087-registration --base MERGE_BASE`) success on the head.
- `service-automation` gains a test file only; no changeset owed there. RIGHT.

### ③ Boundary flags

Deviations in report `6152617434`:
- **Widened file surface (a), three rationale files** (`flow.zod.ts` comment, the step-18 D3 entry, the `registry.ts.template` fragment): ANSWERED. Each sentence became false the moment the carve-out went and feeds the publish-time upgrade guide; shipping the narrowing without them would publish a false rationale. In scope of "the rationale text says what holds"; nothing generated is committed.
- **Widened file surface (b), the `registerFlow` pin in `service-automation/config-parse.test.ts`:** ANSWERED. Triage's pin line reads "the probe is refused at registration at `config.limit`", and registration is `AutomationEngine.registerFlow`, which lives in `service-automation`; the pin is the direction, and the claim's "stop on breach" line was the one in conflict. Named by the dev, accepted by the seat; no escalation.
- **`Clause-②` spelling, claim versus PR:** ANSWERED. The PR body and the changeset carry the gate-readable closed-pair form; closed.
- **Verify-lock queues and three exit-124 runs:** ANSWERED. None reported as a measurement; CI on the head is the reading of record and every suite job is success.
- **Head behind `origin/main`** (4 commits at the report; more now, `origin/main` = `cc14657ed`): ANSWERED. CI's merge-ref run is the reading; the queue re-runs on merge; verified below that no file this diff touches moved on `main` since the merge base.
- **Model-free commit trailers:** ANSWERED. AGENTS.md's prescribed pair; not a contract matter.

`out_of_scope_findings` in the report:
1. **A slot token passes `FlowSchema.parse` / `defineStack` while `registerFlow` and every run refuse it (class a):** ESCALATED already — #23320, filed by the seat at ACCEPT. My reading: this PR keeps parity with `main` at those doors (the carve-out skipped the composed judge issue; exemption 1 skips it now) and makes #23320 no harder — the fix there is for `FlowSchema`'s superRefine to call the two judges, or for the arm to stop exempting at a door that does not call them; either is outside this card. No further action.
2. **A type issue that stays behind the slot judge's verdict until the token is fixed** (a `screen` `title` written as a template envelope): ANSWERED. Identical to `main` (the carve-out hid the same type issue); the judge's refusal is located at the same path, so nothing is silent — the type refusal follows once the token is fixed. Acceptance notes suffice; no card.
3. **The `18.0.0-next.0` CHANGELOG bullet from #21898:** ANSWERED. Release-owned and true when cut; this changeset's FROM → TO supersedes it for the GA notes. Dropped, as the seat ruled.

No flag of my own is blocking.
